translations.literal: Inner and outer offices: those constantly bright number one hundred twenty-four; those that can be named number three hundred twenty; they make two thousand five hundred stars; the count of faint stars is probably eleven thousand five hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Bright stars number 124 named groups, 320 titles, 2,500 visible points, and perhaps 11,520 dimmer ones.

sentences.zh: 庶物蠢蠢，-{咸}-得-{系}-命。

translations.literal: The myriad things teeming, all obtain binding fate.
translations.idiomatic: All creation stirs under threads tied to those lights.

sentences.zh: 不然，何得總而理諸？

translations.literal: If not so, how could they be summed and ordered?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could one chart and govern them?

sentences.zh: 」-{後}-武帝時，太史令陳卓總甘、石、巫-{咸}-三家所著星圖，大凡二百八十三官，一千四百六十四星，以爲定紀。

translations.literal: ” Later, under Wudi, Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo summed the star charts written by Gan, Shi, and Wu Xian—two hundred eighty-three offices in all, one thousand four hundred sixty-four stars—and took them as the fixed canon.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later, under Emperor Wu, Chen Zhuo merged Gan De, Shi Shen, and Wu Xian into 283 constellations and 1,464 stars—the standard star map.

sentences.zh: 今略其昭昭者，以備天官-{云}-。

translations.literal: Now I abbreviate those that are plain, to complete the Offices of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Here I keep the clearest entries for the celestial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 中宮

translations.literal: The Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Palace

sentences.zh: 北極五星，鉤陳六星，皆在紫宮中。

translations.literal: The five stars of the north pole and the six stars of Gouchen are all within the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Five polar stars and six Gouchen stars lie inside the Purple Forbidden enclosure.

sentences.zh: 北極，北辰最尊者也，其紐星，天之樞也。

translations.literal: The north pole is the most honored of northern stars; its pivot star is the pivot of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The pole star is chief of the circumpolar set; its pivot is heaven’s axle.

sentences.zh: 天運無窮，三光迭耀，而極星不移，故曰「居其所而衆星共之」。

translations.literal: Heaven’s motion is without end; the three luminaries shine in turn, yet the pole star does not move; therefore it is said “it dwells in its place and the host of stars submit to it.”
translations.idiomatic: While sun, moon, and stars wheel without rest, the pole holds still—hence the classic says it sits unmoved while others orbit.

sentences.zh: 第一星主月，太子也。

translations.literal: The first star governs the moon, the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The first governs the moon and the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 第二星主日，帝王也；

translations.literal: The second star governs the sun, the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The second governs the sun and the sovereign;

sentences.zh: 亦太乙之坐，謂最赤明者也。

translations.literal: it is also the seat of Grand Unity, called the most red and bright.
translations.idiomatic: it doubles as Taiyi’s throne—the reddest, brightest of the set.

sentences.zh: 第三星主五星，庶子也。

translations.literal: The third star governs the five planets, the son of concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The third presides over the five planets and cadet sons.

sentences.zh: 中星不明，主不用事；

translations.literal: If the middle star is not bright, the ruler does not handle affairs;
translations.idiomatic: A dim middle star means the ruler leaves business undone;

sentences.zh: 右星不明，太子憂。

translations.literal: if the right star is not bright, the heir apparent worries.
translations.idiomatic: a dim right-hand star alarms the heir.

sentences.zh: 鉤陳，-{後}-宮也，大帝之正妃也，大帝之常居也。

translations.literal: Gouchen is the rear palace, the great emperor’s principal consort, the great emperor’s constant residence.
translations.idiomatic: Gouchen is the inner palace—the supreme consort’s quarter and the high god’s dwelling.

sentences.zh: 北四星曰女-{御}-宮，八十一-{御}-妻之象也。

translations.literal: The four northern stars are called the Ladies’ Palace of Attendants, the image of eighty-one attendant wives.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars northward form the concubines’ hall—emblem of the eighty-one consorts.

sentences.zh: 鉤陳口中一星曰天皇大帝，其神曰耀魄寶，主-{御}-群靈，執萬神圖。

translations.literal: The one star in the mouth of Gouchen is called the Celestial Emperor of Grand Heaven; its spirit is called Yaobao; it governs and drives the host of numina and holds the chart of the myriad gods.
translations.idiomatic: The star in Gouchen’s gap is the supreme celestial emperor, spirit-name Yaobao, commander of spirits and keeper of the divine roster.

sentences.zh: 抱北極四星曰四輔，所以輔佐北極而出度授政也。

translations.literal: The four stars embracing the north pole are called the Four Supports, by which they assist the north pole in issuing measures and handing down government.
translations.idiomatic: Four attendants hug the pole—the “four aids” that help it promulgate degrees and policy.

sentences.zh: 大帝上九星曰華蓋，所以覆蔽大帝之坐也。

translations.literal: The nine stars above the great emperor are called Canopy of State, by which they cover and shield the great emperor’s seat.
translations.idiomatic: Nine stars above him form the imperial umbrella, sheltering the throne.

sentences.zh: 蓋下九星曰杠，蓋之柄也。

translations.literal: The nine stars below the canopy are called Gang, the handle of the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Nine stars beneath are the canopy’s shaft.

sentences.zh: 華蓋下五星曰五帝内坐，設敘順帝所居也。

translations.literal: The five stars below the canopy are called the Inner Seats of the Five Thearchs, setting order according to where thearchs dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Five lower stars mark the inner seats of the five cosmic emperors, arrayed by precedence.

sentences.zh: 客星犯紫宮中坐，大臣犯主。

translations.literal: A guest star offending the central seat in the Purple Palace means great ministers offend the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A stray star trespassing the purple throne warns that ministers challenge the king.

sentences.zh: 華蓋杠旁六星曰六甲，可以分陰陽而配節候，故在帝旁，所以布政教而授農時也。

translations.literal: The six stars beside canopy and gang are called the Six Jia; they can divide yin and yang and match seasonal nodes; therefore they are beside the emperor, by which he spreads government and instruction and hands down agricultural seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars flanking canopy and pole are the Six Jia, pairing yin-yang to the seasons so the sovereign can publish the farming calendar.

sentences.zh: 極東一星曰柱下史，主記過；

translations.literal: The one star east of the pole is called the Scribe Below the Pillar, in charge of recording faults;
translations.idiomatic: East of the pole sits the pillar-scribe who logs misdeeds;

sentences.zh: 左右史，此之象也。

translations.literal: left and right scribes—this is their image.
translations.idiomatic: emblem of the left and right historians.

sentences.zh: 柱史北一星曰女史，婦人之微者，主傳漏，故漢有侍史。

translations.literal: North of the pillar scribe one star is called the Woman Scribe, the subtle among women, in charge of transmitting the clepsydra; therefore Han had attendant scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Northward lies the woman scribe, a low-ranking female office that relayed the water-clock—Han kept such attendants.

sentences.zh: 傳-{舍}-九星在華蓋上，近河，賓客之館，主胡人入中國。

translations.literal: The nine stars of the Relay Lodges are on the canopy, near the River; they are the hostel for guests, governing barbarians entering the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Nine “relay lodges” under the canopy by the Milky Way mark the guest quarters—omens of frontier peoples entering China.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，備-{奸}-使，亦曰胡兵起。

translations.literal: When a guest star guards them, prepare against treacherous envoys; also called barbarian troops rising.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star parked there warns of spies or rising barbarian arms.

sentences.zh: 傳-{舍}-南河中五星曰造父，-{御}-官也，一曰司馬，或曰伯樂。

translations.literal: South of the relay lodges in the middle river are five stars called Zaofu, the chariot office; one name is Sima, or Bole.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars south in the river are Zaofu—the chariot bureau, also named Sima or Bole.

sentences.zh: 星亡，馬大貴。

translations.literal: If the stars perish, horses become very expensive.
translations.idiomatic: If they vanish, horse prices soar.

sentences.zh: 其西河中九星如鉤狀，曰鉤星，直則地動。

translations.literal: West in the river nine stars like a hook shape are called Hook Stars; when straight, the earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hook-shaped stars west in the stream are the “hook stars”; when they straighten, expect earthquakes.

sentences.zh: 天一星在紫宮門右星南，天帝之神也，主戰-{鬥}-，知人吉凶者也。

translations.literal: The one star Heaven-One is south of the right star at the Purple Palace gate; it is the spirit of the Celestial Thearch, governs warfare, and knows people’s fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-One sits just inside the purple gate—god of battle and augury of weal and woe.

sentences.zh: 太一星在天一南，相近，亦天帝神也，主使十六神，知風雨水旱、兵革饑謹、疾疫災害所在之國也。

translations.literal: Grand-One is south of Heaven-One, close by; it is also a spirit of the Celestial Thearch, governs dispatching sixteen spirits, and knows in which states lie wind, rain, flood or drought, arms, famine, pestilence, and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Grand-One hugs Heaven-One, commanding sixteen emissaries to spy out storms, war, famine, and plague in every realm.

sentences.zh: 紫宮垣十五星，其西番七，東番八，在北-{斗}-北。

translations.literal: The Purple Palace wall fifteen stars: its western battalion seven, eastern battalion eight, north of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The purple wall counts fifteen stars—seven west, eight east—arching north of the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 一曰紫微，大帝之坐也，天子之常居也，主命主度也。

translations.literal: One name is Purple Subtlety, the great emperor’s seat, the Son of Heaven’s constant residence; it governs fate and governs measures.
translations.idiomatic: Called Purple Tenuity, it is the high god’s throne and the emperor’s home, ruling fate and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 一曰長垣，一曰天營，一曰旗星，爲番衞，備番臣也。

translations.literal: One name is Long Wall, one name is Heavenly Camp, one name is Banner Stars; they are rotating guards, preparing rotating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Also dubbed Long Rampart, Heavenly Camp, and Banner Stars—the rotating watch of palace guards.

sentences.zh: 宮闕兵起，旗星直，天子出，自將宮中兵。

translations.literal: When palace gates see troops rising, if banner stars are straight, the Son of Heaven goes out, personally leading palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: If rebellion stirs the palace and the banner stars line up straight, the emperor will ride out at the head of his household army.

sentences.zh: 東垣下五星曰天柱，建政教，懸圖法。

translations.literal: The five stars below the eastern wall are called Heavenly Pillars, establishing government and instruction, hanging charts and laws.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars under the east wall are the Heavenly Pillars—where edicts and law codes are posted.

sentences.zh: 門内東南維五星曰尚書，主納言，夙夜諮謀；

translations.literal: Five stars at the inner southeast corner of the gate are called Masters of Writing, in charge of receiving words, consulting day and night;
translations.idiomatic: Five stars in the gate’s southeast pocket are the Masters of Writing, who take memorials and counsel night and day;

sentences.zh: 龍作納言，此之象也。

translations.literal: Long serving as receiver of words—this is their image.
translations.idiomatic: the model of the dragon minister who “received words” for the throne.

sentences.zh: 尚書西二星曰陰德、陽德，主周急振撫。

translations.literal: West of Masters of Writing two stars are called Yin Power and Yang Power, in charge of urgent relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars west are Yin De and Yang De, stars of emergency relief.

sentences.zh: 宮門左星内二星曰大理，主平刑斷獄也。

translations.literal: Two stars inside the left gate star are called Grand Pattern, in charge of leveling punishments and judging cases.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the left gate sit two stars of Grand Rectitude, emblems of fair trials.

sentences.zh: 門外六星曰天床，主寢-{舍}-，解息燕休。

translations.literal: Six stars outside the gate are called Heavenly Couch, in charge of sleeping quarters, loosening rest, swallow feasts, and repose.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars outside mark the Heavenly Couch—the celestial bedchamber for rest and banquet.

sentences.zh: 西南角外二星曰内廚，主六宮之内飲食，主-{后}-妃夫人與太子宴飲。

translations.literal: Two stars outside the southwest corner are called Inner Kitchen; they govern drink and food within the six palaces, governing empress, consorts, and feasting with the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars past the southwest corner are the Inner Kitchen, provisioning the inner palaces and the banquets of empress, ladies, and crown prince.

sentences.zh: 東北維外六星曰天廚，主盛饌。

translations.literal: Six stars outside the northeast corner are called Heavenly Kitchen; they govern lavish fare.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars beyond the northeast corner form the Heavenly Kitchen, the court of grand feasts.

sentences.zh: 北-{斗}-七星在太微北，七政之樞機，陰陽之元本也。

translations.literal: The seven stars of the Northern Dipper are north of Supreme Subtlety; they are the pivot of the seven regulators, the root origin of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Purple Palace rise the Dipper’s seven stars—the hinge of the seven governors and the wellspring of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 故運乎天中，而臨-{制}-四方，以建四時，而均五行也。

translations.literal: Therefore they revolve in the midst of Heaven and oversee and control the four quarters, thereby establishing the four seasons and balancing the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: They wheel at heaven’s hub, commanding the four directions, pacing the seasons, and tuning the five phases.

sentences.zh: 魁四星爲旋璣，杓三星爲玉衡。

translations.literal: The four stars of the bowl are the Rotating Pearl Armillary; the three stars of the handle are the Jade Traverse.
translations.idiomatic: The bowl is the “pearl pivot,” the handle the “jade sight-bar” of classical lore.

sentences.zh: 又曰，-{斗}-爲人君之象，號令之主也。

translations.literal: Again it is said the Dipper is the image of the human lord, master of commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper also stands for the ruler, source of all edicts.

sentences.zh: 又爲帝車，取乎運動之義也。

translations.literal: Again it is the Emperor’s Chariot, taking the meaning of motion.
translations.idiomatic: It is styled the imperial chariot—ever in motion.

sentences.zh: 又魁第一星曰天樞，二曰璿，三曰璣，四曰權，五曰玉衡，六曰開陽，七曰搖光，一至四爲魁，五至七爲杓。

translations.literal: Again, the first star of the bowl is called Celestial Pivot, second Xuan, third Ji, fourth Quan, fifth Jade Traverse, sixth Kaiyang, seventh Yaoguang; one through four are the bowl, five through seven the handle.
translations.idiomatic: Their names run Pivot, Xuan, Ji, Quan, Jade Balance, Kaiyang, and Yaoguang—four in the Dipper cup, three in the shaft.

sentences.zh: 樞爲天，璿爲地，璣爲人，權爲時，玉衡爲音，開陽爲律，搖光爲星。

translations.literal: Pivot is Heaven, Xuan is Earth, Ji is Man, Quan is Season, Jade Traverse is Sound, Kaiyang is Pitch-pipe, Yaoguang is Star.
translations.idiomatic: Each star maps a cosmic note: heaven, earth, man, season, tone, pitch-standard, and the wandering spark.

sentences.zh: 石氏-{云}-：「第一曰正星，主陽德，天子之象也。

translations.literal: The Shi family said: “The first is called Correct Star, governing yang virtue, the image of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shen names the first the Correct Star of yang virtue—the emperor’s star.

sentences.zh: 二曰法星，主陰刑，女主之位也。

translations.literal: The second is called Law Star, governing yin punishments, the position of the chief consort.
translations.idiomatic: The second is the Law Star of yin penalties—the empress’s seat.

sentences.zh: 三曰令星，主中禍。

translations.literal: The third is called Command Star, governing inner calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The third is the Command Star of palace misfortune.

sentences.zh: 四曰伐星，主天理，伐無道。

translations.literal: The fourth is called Punitive Star, governing Heaven’s pattern, punishing the lawless.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth is the Punitive Star that executes heaven’s justice on the wicked.

sentences.zh: 五曰殺星，主中央，助四旁，殺有罪。

translations.literal: The fifth is called Slaughter Star, governing the center, assisting the four sides, executing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth is the Slaughter Star at the hub, aiding the four quarters in killing criminals.

sentences.zh: 六曰危星，主天倉五-{穀}-。

translations.literal: The sixth is called Peril Star, governing Heaven’s granary and the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth is the Peril Star over heaven’s granaries and the five grains.

sentences.zh: 七曰部星，亦曰應星，主兵。

translations.literal: The seventh is called Department Star, also called Responsive Star, governing arms.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh is the Department or Response Star, master of war.

sentences.zh: 」又-{云}-：「一主天，二主地，三主火，四主水，五主土，六主木，七主金。

translations.literal: ” Again it said: “One governs Heaven, two Earth, three Fire, four Water, five Earth, six Wood, seven Metal.
translations.idiomatic: ” Another list ties them to heaven, earth, fire, water, soil, wood, and metal.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「一主秦，二主楚，三主梁，四主呉，五主燕，六主趙，七主齊。」

translations.literal: ” Again it said: “One governs Qin, two Chu, three Liang, four Wu, five Yan, six Zhao, seven Qi.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet another matches them to Qin, Chu, Liang, Wu, Yan, Zhao, and Qi.”

sentences.zh: 魁中四星爲貴人之牢，曰天理也。

translations.literal: The four stars within the bowl are the prison of honorable men, called Heavenly Pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The cup’s inner four are the nobles’ jail, named Heavenly Pattern.

sentences.zh: 輔星傅乎開陽，所以佐-{斗}-成功，丞相之象也。

translations.literal: The companion star cleaves to Kaiyang, thereby assisting the Dipper to success; it is the image of the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The companion hugging Kaiyang helps the Dipper finish its work—the chancellor’s star.

sentences.zh: 七政星明，其國昌；

translations.literal: When the seven regulator stars are bright, that state flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: Bright regulator stars mean a thriving realm;

sentences.zh: 輔星明，則臣強。

translations.literal: when the companion star is bright, ministers are strong.
translations.idiomatic: a brilliant companion star signals powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 杓南三星及魁第一星西三星皆曰三公，主宜德化，調七政，和陰陽之官也。

translations.literal: The three stars south of the handle and the three stars west of the first star of the bowl are all called the Three Dukes, governing fitting virtue and transformation, harmonizing the seven regulators, officials who harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars south of the handle plus three west of the bowl’s first are the Three Dukes, ministers who tune policy, the seven governors, and yin-yang.

sentences.zh: 文昌六星，在北-{斗}-魁前，天之六府也，主集計天道。

translations.literal: The six stars of Literary Glory are before the Northern Dipper’s bowl; they are Heaven’s six treasuries, governing gathering and reckoning Heaven’s way.
translations.idiomatic: Six Wenchang stars before the Dipper bowl are heaven’s six bureaus of audit and planning.

sentences.zh: 一曰上將，大將軍建威武。

translations.literal: The first is called Supreme General, grand general establishing awe and might.
translations.idiomatic: First is the Supreme General who raises military majesty.

sentences.zh: 二曰次將，尚書正左右。

translations.literal: The second is called Next General, Masters of Writing rectifying left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Second is the Vice General paired with the Masters of Writing who keep the court in line.

sentences.zh: 三曰貴相，太常理文緒。

translations.literal: The third is called Honored Minister, grand minister of rituals ordering literary threads.
translations.idiomatic: Third is the Honored Minister, grand steward of rites and records.

sentences.zh: 四曰司祿、司中，司隸賞功進。

translations.literal: The fourth is called Director of Emoluments and Director of the Center, director of convicts rewarding merit and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth pairs Director of Emoluments and Director of the Center—overseeing rewards and promotions.

sentences.zh: 五曰司命、司怪，太史主滅咎。

translations.literal: The fifth is called Director of Fate and Director of Prodigies, grand scribe in charge of quelling blame.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth joins Director of Fate and Director of Portents—the grand scribe who lifts blame from the throne.

sentences.zh: 六曰司寇，大理佐理寶。

translations.literal: The sixth is called Director of Bandits, grand pattern assisting in managing treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth is the Director of Bandits with the grand judge, guarding the royal treasury.

sentences.zh: 所謂一者，起北-{斗}-魁前近内階者也。

translations.literal: What is called the first is that which rises before the Northern Dipper’s bowl near the inner steps.
translations.idiomatic: The “first” is the star nearest the inner stair before the Dipper bowl.

sentences.zh: 明潤，大小齊，天瑞臻。

translations.literal: Bright and lustrous, sizes even—Heaven’s auspicious omens arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When they shine evenly, heaven sends its felicitous signs.

sentences.zh: 文昌北六星曰内階，天皇之階也。

translations.literal: Six stars north of Literary Glory are called Inner Steps, the steps of the Celestial Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars north of Wenchang are the Inner Steps of the high god.

sentences.zh: 相一星在北-{斗}-南。

translations.literal: One star called Minister is south of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister star stands just south of the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 相者，總領百司而掌邦教，以佐帝王安邦國，集衆事也。

translations.literal: The minister is one who overall leads the hundred offices and holds state instruction in hand, thereby assisting the emperor to stabilize the state and gather the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He is the chief who runs every bureau, teaches the realm, and steadies the throne.

sentences.zh: 其星明，吉。

translations.literal: When its star is bright, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: A bright Minister star is good omen.

sentences.zh: 太陽守一星，在相西，大將大臣之象也，主戒不虞，設武備。

translations.literal: The one star Great Yang Guard is west of Minister, the image of great generals and great ministers, governing guarding against the unexpected and setting martial readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yang Guard west of him is the star of marshals and ministers on alert, keeping arms ready.

sentences.zh: 西北四星曰勢。

translations.literal: Four stars in the northwest are called Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Four northwest stars are Shi.

sentences.zh: 勢，腐刑人也。

translations.literal: Shi means the mutilated punishment man.
translations.idiomatic: They image the palace eunuch guard.

sentences.zh: 天牢六星，在北-{斗}-魁下，貴人之牢也。

translations.literal: The six stars of Heavenly Prison are below the Northern Dipper’s bowl, the prison of honorable men.
translations.idiomatic: Six Heavenly Prison stars under the Dipper bowl are the nobles’ lockup.

sentences.zh: 太微，天子庭也，五帝之坐也，十二諸侯府也。

translations.literal: Supreme Subtlety is the Son of Heaven’s courtyard, the seats of the Five Thearchs, the offices of the twelve feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the emperor’s court, the five thrones, and the twelve feudatories.

sentences.zh: 其外蕃，九卿也。

translations.literal: Its outer battalions are the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Its outer ramparts stand for the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 一曰太微爲衡。

translations.literal: One name is that Supreme Subtlety is the beam-scale.
translations.idiomatic: It is also called the celestial balance-beam.

sentences.zh: 衡，主平也。

translations.literal: The beam-scale governs leveling.
translations.idiomatic: That beam means equity.

sentences.zh: 又爲天庭，理法平辭，監升授德，列宿受符，諸神考節，舒情稽疑也。

translations.literal: Again it is the celestial court, ordering law and leveling pleas, supervising promotion and conferring virtue, lodges receiving tallies, spirits examining nodes, expressing feeling and examining doubts.
translations.idiomatic: It is heaven’s courtroom—where law is weighed, merit raised, tallies issued, spirits check timing, and doubts are tried.

sentences.zh: 南蕃中二星間曰端門。

translations.literal: Between the two stars in the middle of the southern battalion is called the Straight Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The gap between the two southern wall stars is the Straight Gate.

sentences.zh: 東曰左執法，廷尉之象也。

translations.literal: East is called Left Law Enforcer, image of the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: East of it is the Left Law Enforcer—the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 西曰右執法，-{御}-史大夫之象也。

translations.literal: West is called Right Law Enforcer, image of the imperial counselor.
translations.idiomatic: West is the Right Law Enforcer—the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 執法，所以舉刺凶-{奸}-者也。

translations.literal: Law enforcers are what raise and impeach the vicious and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Those stars impeach treason and vice.

sentences.zh: 左執法之東，左掖門也。

translations.literal: East of the left law enforcer is the left side gate.
translations.idiomatic: East of the left enforcer lies the left flanking gate.

sentences.zh: 右執法之西，右掖門也。

translations.literal: West of the right law enforcer is the right side gate.
translations.idiomatic: West of the right enforcer is the right flanking gate.

sentences.zh: 東蕃四星，南第一星曰上相，其北，東太陽門；

translations.literal: The eastern battalion four stars: the southern first is called supreme minister; north of it is the east great-yang gate;
translations.idiomatic: The eastern wall’s southernmost is the supreme minister; northward opens the east great-yang gate;

sentences.zh: 第二星曰次相，其北，中華東門也；

translations.literal: the second star is called next minister; north of it is the central splendor east gate;
translations.idiomatic: the next is the vice minister with the central splendor east gate north of it;

sentences.zh: 第三星曰次將，其北，東太陰門也；

translations.literal: the third star is called next general; north of it is the east great-yin gate;
translations.idiomatic: the third is the vice general beside the east great-yin gate;

sentences.zh: 第四星曰上將：所謂四輔也。

translations.literal: the fourth star is called supreme general: these are called the four supports.
translations.idiomatic: the fourth is the supreme general—the eastern “four supports.”

sentences.zh: 西蕃四星，南第一星曰上將，其北，西太陽門也；

translations.literal: The western battalion four stars: the southern first is called supreme general; north of it is the west great-yang gate;
translations.idiomatic: The western wall’s southern star is the supreme general with the west great-yang gate;

sentences.zh: 第二星曰次將，其北，中華西門也；

translations.literal: the second star is called next general; north of it is the central splendor west gate;
translations.idiomatic: next comes the vice general and central splendor west gate;

sentences.zh: 第三星曰次相，其北，西太陰門也；

translations.literal: the third star is called next minister; north of it is the west great-yin gate;
translations.idiomatic: then the vice minister and west great-yin gate;

sentences.zh: 第四曰上相：亦曰四輔也。

translations.literal: the fourth is called supreme minister: also called the four supports.
translations.idiomatic: last is the supreme minister—again the four supports.

sentences.zh: 東西蕃有芒及動搖者，諸侯謀。

translations.literal: When east and west battalions have awns and shake, the feudal lords plot.
translations.idiomatic: Comets or tremors on those walls mean the nobles are plotting.

sentences.zh: 執法移，刑罰尤急。

translations.literal: When law enforcers shift, punishments are especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: If the law stars drift, justice turns harsh.

sentences.zh: 月、五星入太微，軌道，吉。

translations.literal: When moon and five planets enter Supreme Subtlety on their tracks, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Moon and five wanderers crossing the enclosure on proper paths bring good fortune.

sentences.zh: 其所犯中坐，成刑。

translations.literal: That which they offend at the central seat completes punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Trespass on the central throne completes a sentence of fate.

sentences.zh: 其西南角外三星曰明堂，天子布政之宮。

translations.literal: Three stars outside its southwest corner are called Bright Hall, the palace where the Son of Heaven spreads government.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars past the southwest corner are the Bright Hall where the emperor publishes policy.

sentences.zh: 明堂西三星曰靈-{臺}-，觀-{臺}-也，主觀-{雲}-物，察符瑞，候災變也。

translations.literal: Three stars west of Bright Hall are called Spirit Terrace, observatory towers, governing observing clouds and things, examining tallies and omens, waiting on disasters and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: West of them stand three Spirit Terrace stars—the observatory that reads clouds, omens, and portents.

sentences.zh: 左執法東北一星曰謁者，主贊賓客也。

translations.literal: One star northeast of the left law enforcer is called Usher, governing assisting guests.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the left enforcer is the Usher who greets envoys.

sentences.zh: 謁者東北三星曰三公内坐，朝會之所居也。

translations.literal: Three stars northeast of Usher are called Inner Seats of the Three Dukes, where court meetings dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars beyond are the inner seats of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 三公北三星曰九卿内坐，治萬事。

translations.literal: Three stars north of the Three Dukes are called Inner Seats of the Nine Ministers, ordering the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: North of them sit the Nine Ministers’ inner bench, running every department.

sentences.zh: 九卿西五星曰内五諸侯，内待天子，不之國也。

translations.literal: Five stars west of the Nine Ministers are called Inner Five Feudatories, attending the Son of Heaven within and not going to their states.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars westward are the inner marquises who stay at court instead of their fiefs.

sentences.zh: -{辟}-雍之禮得，則太微、諸侯明。

translations.literal: When the rites of the Biyong are obtained, then Supreme Subtlety and the feudal lords are bright.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban academy rites are correct, the enclosure and feudatory stars shine clear.

sentences.zh: 黃帝坐在太微中，含樞紐之神也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Thearch’s seat is within Supreme Subtlety, the spirit of Han-shu pivot.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Thearch’s throne lies within—the spirit called Han-shu pivot.

sentences.zh: 天子動得天度，止得地意，從容中道，則太微五帝坐明以光。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven moves he obtains Heaven’s measure, when he stops he obtains Earth’s intent, easeful in the middle way, then the five thearch seats of Supreme Subtlety are bright with light.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler moves with heaven’s gauge, rests with earth’s mind, and walks the middle way, the five thrones blaze.

sentences.zh: 黃帝坐不明，人主求賢士以輔法，不然則奪勢。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Thearch’s seat is not bright, the human lord seeks worthy scholars to assist the law; if not, then power is wrested.
translations.idiomatic: A dim yellow throne drives the king to seek wise counsel—or lose his mandate.

sentences.zh: 四帝星夾黃帝坐，東方蒼帝，靈威仰之神也；

translations.literal: The four thearch stars flank the Yellow Thearch’s seat: east the Green Thearch, spirit of Ling-weiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Four thrones ring the yellow seat—east the Green Thearch Ling-weiyang;

sentences.zh: 南方赤帝，赤熛怒之神也；

translations.literal: south the Red Thearch, spirit of Red-blazing wrath;
translations.idiomatic: south the Red Thearch of blazing wrath;

sentences.zh: 西方白帝，白招矩之神也；

translations.literal: west the White Thearch, spirit of White-summoning measure;
translations.idiomatic: west the White Thearch who summons order;

sentences.zh: 北方黑帝，-{葉}-光紀之神也。

translations.literal: north the Black Thearch, spirit of Ye-light-order.
translations.idiomatic: north the Black Thearch of leaf-light record.

sentences.zh: 五帝坐北一星曰太子，帝儲也。

translations.literal: One star north of the five thearch seats is called Heir Apparent, the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: North of the five thrones shines the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子北一星曰從官，侍臣也。

translations.literal: One star north of Heir Apparent is called Attendant, a serving minister.
translations.idiomatic: North again is the Attendant courtier.

sentences.zh: 帝坐東北一星曰幸臣。

translations.literal: One star northeast of the imperial seat is called Favorite Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the throne sits the Favorite Minister.

sentences.zh: 屛四星在端門之内，近右執法。

translations.literal: Four stars of the screen are inside the Straight Gate, near the right law enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Four Screen stars inside the Straight Gate hug the right enforcer.

sentences.zh: 屛，所以雍蔽學帝也。

translations.literal: The screen is what blocks and screens, learning of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They veil the private audience with the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 執法主刺舉；

translations.literal: Law enforcers govern impeachment;
translations.idiomatic: The law stars handle denunciation;

sentences.zh: 臣尊敬君上，則星光明潤澤。

translations.literal: when ministers revere and respect the ruler above, then the stars are bright, moist, and lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: when ministers honor the throne, those stars burn clear and mild.

sentences.zh: 郎位十五星在帝坐東北。

translations.literal: Fifteen stars of Gentlemen of the Palace are northeast of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Gentlemen of the Palace stars cluster northeast of the throne.

sentences.zh: 一曰依烏郎府也。

translations.literal: One name is the crow-roost gentlemen’s office.
translations.idiomatic: They are also called the crow-roost cadet corps.

sentences.zh: 周官之元士，漢官之光祿、中散、諫議、議郎、三署郎中，是其職也。

translations.literal: They are the primordial shi of Zhou offices, Han offices of radiant emolument, palace attendant, remonstrator, deliberation gentleman, and gentlemen of the three bureaus—these are their duties.
translations.idiomatic: They match Zhou cadets and Han gentlemen of the palace, remonstrance, and deliberation bureaus.

sentences.zh: 郎，主守衞也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen govern guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Those stars mean palace watch.

sentences.zh: 其星不具，-{后}-妃死，幸臣誅。

translations.literal: When the stars are not complete, the empress dies, favorite ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: If the constellation breaks, expect death of the empress and execution of favorites.

sentences.zh: 星明大及客星入之，大臣爲亂。

translations.literal: When the stars are bright and large or a guest star enters them, great ministers make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden brilliance or a guest star there signals ministerial revolt.

sentences.zh: 郎將在郎位北，主閲具，所以爲武備也。

translations.literal: Gentleman-general is north of Gentlemen of the Palace, governing inspection of readiness, thereby serving as martial preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The captain of gentlemen north of them inspects readiness for war.

sentences.zh: 武賁一星，在太微西蕃北，下-{臺}-南，靜室旄頭之騎官也。

translations.literal: One star Martial Splendor is north of the western battalion of Supreme Subtlety, south of the lower terrace, the riding office of still chamber plume-head.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Splendor rides north of the western wall, south of the lower terrace—the plume-helmet guard.

sentences.zh: 常陳七星，如畢狀，在帝坐北，天子宿衞武賁之士，以設強-{禦}-也。

translations.literal: Seven stars of Ever-array, shaped like the Net, are north of the imperial seat, gentlemen of the Son of Heaven’s night guard and martial splendor, thereby setting strong defense.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Ever-array stars like a net north of the throne are the night guard of martial gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 星搖動，天子自出，明則武兵用，微則兵弱。

translations.literal: When the stars shake, the Son of Heaven goes out himself; when bright, martial troops are used; when faint, troops are weak.
translations.idiomatic: Their tremor means the emperor leads his host; brightness means war; dimness means a feeble army.

sentences.zh: 三-{台}-六星，兩兩而居，起文昌，列抵太微。

translations.literal: Six stars of the Three Terraces, dwelling two by two, rise from Literary Glory and range to Supreme Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Six Three-Terrace stars in three pairs run from Wenchang toward the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 一曰天住，三公之位也。

translations.literal: One name is Celestial Stay, the position of the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: They are called the Celestial Lodging of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 在人曰三公，在天曰三-{台}-，主開德宜符也。

translations.literal: Among people they are the three dukes; in Heaven they are the three terraces, governing opening virtue and fitting tallies.
translations.idiomatic: On earth they are the three dukes; in the sky the three steps that align virtue with heaven’s signs.

sentences.zh: 西近文昌二星曰上-{台}-，爲司命，主壽。

translations.literal: Two stars west near Literary Glory are called Upper Terrace, being Director of Fate, governing longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The pair nearest Wenchang is the Upper Terrace—Director of Fate and length of life.

sentences.zh: 次二星曰中-{台}-，爲司中，主宗室。

translations.literal: The next two stars are called Middle Terrace, being Director of the Center, governing the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The next pair is the Middle Terrace—Director of the Center over the royal house.

sentences.zh: 東二星曰下-{台}-，爲司祿，主兵，所以昭德塞違也。

translations.literal: The eastern two stars are called Lower Terrace, being Director of Emoluments, governing arms, thereby displaying virtue and blocking transgression.
translations.idiomatic: The easternmost pair is the Lower Terrace—Director of Emoluments and war, sealing virtue and blocking fault.

sentences.zh: 又曰三-{台}-爲天階，太一躡以上下。

translations.literal: Again it is said the Three Terraces are Heaven’s stairway, whereby Grand Unity treads up and down.
translations.idiomatic: They are also called heaven’s staircase, which Taiyi mounts and descends.

sentences.zh: 一曰泰階。

translations.literal: One name is Grand Stairway.
translations.idiomatic: Another name is the Great Steps.

sentences.zh: 上階，上星爲天子，下星爲女主；

translations.literal: Upper stair: upper star is the Son of Heaven, lower star is the chief consort;
translations.idiomatic: On the upper step the upper lamp is the emperor, the lower the empress;

sentences.zh: 中階，上星爲諸侯三公，下星爲卿大夫；

translations.literal: middle stair: upper star is the feudal lords and three dukes, lower star is ministers and grandees;
translations.idiomatic: on the middle step the upper is the nobles and three dukes, the lower the ministers;

sentences.zh: 下階，上星爲士，下星爲庶人：所以和陰陽而理萬物也。

translations.literal: lower stair: upper star is shi, lower star is commoners: by this means harmonizing yin and yang and ordering the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: on the lower step the upper is the gentry, the lower the common folk—together they tune yin and yang and order the world.

sentences.zh: 君臣和集，如其常度，有變則占其人。

translations.literal: When lord and ministers gather in harmony like their constant measure, if there is change then one divines the person.
translations.idiomatic: When court and throne hold their usual brightness, any flicker tells which rank is at fault.

sentences.zh: 南四星曰内平，近職執法平罪之官也。

translations.literal: Four southern stars are called Inner Level, officials near duty who enforce the law and level crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Four southern stars are the Inner Tribunal—judges who balance punishments beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 中-{台}-之北一星曰太尊，貴戚也。

translations.literal: One star north of the middle terrace is called Grand Esteem, honored kin.
translations.idiomatic: North of the middle pair shines Grand Esteem—the imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 攝提六星，直-{斗}-杓之南，主建時節，伺禨祥。

translations.literal: Six stars of Sheti, straight south of the Dipper’s handle, govern establishing seasonal nodes and watching omens.
translations.idiomatic: Six Sheti stars guard the handle’s south, fixing the seasons and reading portents.

sentences.zh: 攝提爲楯，以夾擁帝座也，主九卿。

translations.literal: Sheti is a shield, thereby embracing and flanking the imperial seat; it governs the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They form a buckler bracketing the throne and stand for the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 明大，三公恣。

translations.literal: Bright and large—the three dukes act willfully.
translations.idiomatic: If they blaze large, the three dukes grow overbearing.

sentences.zh: 客星入之，聖人受-{制}-。

translations.literal: When a guest star enters them, a sage ruler suffers constraint.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star there means the sovereign falls under another’s power.

sentences.zh: 西三星曰周鼎，主流亡。

translations.literal: Three western stars are called Zhou Tripods, governing exile and wandering.
translations.idiomatic: Three western stars are the Zhou cauldrons—omens of exile and drift.

sentences.zh: 大角在攝提間。

translations.literal: Great Horn lies between Sheti.
translations.idiomatic: Arcturus rides between the Sheti hooks.

sentences.zh: 大角者，天王座也。

translations.literal: Great Horn is the seat of the celestial king.
translations.idiomatic: That lamp is the throne of the celestial king.

sentences.zh: 又爲天棟，正經紀也。

translations.literal: Again it is Heaven’s Ridgepole, rectifying the warp and woof.
translations.idiomatic: It is heaven’s roof-beam, setting the cosmic grid.

sentences.zh: 北三星曰帝席，主宴獻酬酢。

translations.literal: Three stars north are called Imperial Mat, governing feasting, toasts, and pledges.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars north are the emperor’s banquet mat for pledging cups.

sentences.zh: 北三星曰梗河，天矛也。

translations.literal: Three stars north are called Geng River, Heaven’s spear.
translations.idiomatic: Three more north are Geng River—the sky’s spear.

sentences.zh: 一曰天鋒，主胡兵。

translations.literal: One name is Heaven’s Point, governing Hu troops.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the heaven-spear, it tracks northern armies.

sentences.zh: 又爲喪，故其變動應以兵喪也。

translations.literal: Again it governs mourning; therefore its changes answer to arms and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: It also spells mourning, so its shifts pair war with death.

sentences.zh: 星亡，其國有兵謀。

translations.literal: When the star perishes, that state has military plotting.
translations.idiomatic: If it vanishes, a realm is plotting war.

sentences.zh: 其北一星曰招搖，一曰矛楯，其北一星曰玄戈，皆主胡兵，占與梗河略相類也。

translations.literal: One star north is called Yaoguang, one name spear-shield; one star north is called Dark Lance; all govern Hu troops; divination is broadly like Geng River.
translations.idiomatic: North stand Yaoguang and Dark Lance—more Hu-war omens, read like Geng River.

sentences.zh: 招搖與北-{斗}-杓間曰天庫。

translations.literal: Between Yaoguang and the Northern Dipper’s handle is called Heaven’s Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yaoguang and the Dipper handle lies the celestial granary.

sentences.zh: 星去其所，則有庫開之祥也。

translations.literal: When a star leaves its place, there is the auspice of the storehouse opening.
translations.idiomatic: A star straying from place means the granary gates swing open—relief or peril.

sentences.zh: 招搖欲與棟星、梗河、北-{斗}-相應，則胡兵當來受命-{於}-中國。

translations.literal: When Yaoguang wishes to respond to Ridgepole Star, Geng River, and the Northern Dipper, then Hu troops will come to receive orders from the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang aligns with the ridge star, Geng River, and Dipper, northern hosts will submit to China.

sentences.zh: 玄戈又主北夷，客星守之，胡大敗。

translations.literal: Dark Lance again governs northern Yi; when a guest star guards it, the Hu suffer great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Dark Lance also rules northern tribes; a guest star parked on it foretells their rout.

sentences.zh: 天槍三星，在北-{斗}-杓東，一曰天鉞，天之武備也。

translations.literal: Three stars of Heaven’s Lance are east of the Northern Dipper’s handle; one name is Heaven’s Axe, Heaven’s martial readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Three “Heaven’s Lance” stars east of the handle—heaven’s battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 故在紫宮之左，所以-{禦}-難也。

translations.literal: Therefore they are left of the Purple Palace, thereby guarding against calamity.
translations.idiomatic: They stand left of the purple court as shields against disaster.

sentences.zh: 女床三星，在紀星北，-{後}-宮-{御}-也，主女事。

translations.literal: Three stars of Woman’s Couch are north of the Cord Star, the rear palace attendants, governing women’s affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three Woman’s Couch stars north of Cord govern the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 天棓五星，在女床北，天子先驅也，主分爭與刑罰，藏兵亦所以-{禦}-難也。

translations.literal: Five stars of Heaven’s Club are north of Woman’s Couch, the Son of Heaven’s outriders, governing division, quarrel, and punishments; storing arms is also thereby guarding against calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Five Heaven’s Club stars north of the couch are the sovereign’s outriders—strife, sentence, and stored arms against sudden peril.

sentences.zh: 槍、棓，皆以備非常也；

translations.literal: Lance and club are both to prepare for the extraordinary;
translations.idiomatic: Lance and club both brace for the unexpected;

sentences.zh: 一星不具，其國兵起。

translations.literal: when one star is not complete, that state’s troops rise.
translations.idiomatic: if any star is missing, armies rise in the matching region.

sentences.zh: 東七星曰扶筐，盛桑之器，主勸蠶也。

translations.literal: Seven eastern stars are called Basket Support, vessels for mulberry, governing encouraging silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: Seven eastern Basket stars are mulberry baskets—stars that urge sericulture.

sentences.zh: 七公七星，在招搖東，天之相也，三公之象也，主七政。

translations.literal: Seven stars of Seven Lords are east of Yaoguang, Heaven’s minister, image of the three dukes, governing the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Lords east of Yaoguang image the chief minister and the seven regulators.

sentences.zh: 貫索九星在其前，賤人之牢也。

translations.literal: Nine stars of Coiled Rope are before them, the prison of mean men.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Coiled Rope stars ahead are the commoners’ jail.

sentences.zh: 一曰連索，一曰連營，一曰天牢，主法律，禁暴強也。

translations.literal: One name is Linked Rope, one name Linked Camp, one name Heaven’s Prison, governing law, forbidding violence and the strong.
translations.idiomatic: Called linked rope, linked camp, or heaven’s prison—law that curbs the violent.

sentences.zh: 牢口一星爲門，欲其開也。

translations.literal: One star at the prison’s mouth is the gate; one desires it to open.
translations.idiomatic: The mouth star is the gate—astrologers wish it open for mercy.

sentences.zh: 九星皆明，天下獄煩；

translations.literal: When all nine stars are bright, prisons are numerous under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: When all nine blaze, dungeons crowd the realm;

sentences.zh: 七星見，小赦；

translations.literal: when seven appear, small amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: when only seven show, a small amnesty;

sentences.zh: 六星、五星，大赦。

translations.literal: six stars, five stars, great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: six or five visible, a great pardon.

sentences.zh: 動則斧鑕用，中空則更元。

translations.literal: When they move then axe and adze are used; when hollow in the center then the first year changes.
translations.idiomatic: Motion means executions; a hollow center means the dynasty turns.

translations.literal: The Han treatise said fifteen stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Han monograph counted fifteen stars here.

sentences.zh: 天紀九星，在貫索東，九卿也，主萬事之紀，理怨訟也。

translations.literal: Nine stars of Heaven’s Record are east of Coiled Rope, the nine ministers, governing the record of the myriad affairs and ordering resentful lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Heaven’s Record stars east of the rope are the nine ministers who archive affairs and hear grievances.

sentences.zh: 明則天下多辭訟；

translations.literal: When bright, under Heaven there are many lawsuits;
translations.idiomatic: Brightness means litigation floods the land;

sentences.zh: 亡則政理壞，國紀亂；

translations.literal: when gone, government is ruined and state records are chaotic;
translations.idiomatic: extinction means broken government and tangled statutes;

sentences.zh: 散絶則地震山崩。

translations.literal: scattered and cut off then earthquake and mountain collapse.
translations.idiomatic: scattered breakup means quakes and falling peaks.

sentences.zh: 織女三星，在天紀東端，天女也，主果蓏絲帛珍寶也。

translations.literal: Three stars of the Weaving Girl are at the east end of Heaven’s Record, the celestial maiden, governing fruits, silks, bolts, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Three Weaving Maid stars at the record’s east end govern fruit, silk, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 王者至孝，神祗-{咸}-喜，則織女星倶明，天下和平。

translations.literal: When the king is supremely filial, spirits and gods are all pleased, then the Weaving Maid stars are all bright and under Heaven is peace.
translations.idiomatic: Perfect filial piety lights all three stars and brings peace.

sentences.zh: 大星怒角，布帛貴。

translations.literal: When the great star is angry with horns, cloth and silk are dear.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief star bristles, cloth grows costly.

sentences.zh: 東足四星曰漸-{臺}-，臨水之-{臺}-也，主晷漏律呂之事。

translations.literal: Four stars at the eastern foot are called Gradual Terrace, terraces by water, governing gnomon shadow, clepsydra, pitch-pipes, and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars on the eastern foot are Gradual Terraces by the water—timekeeping and pitch.

sentences.zh: 西足五星曰輦道，王者得嬉-{遊}-之道也，漢輦道通南北宮，其象也。

translations.literal: Five stars at the western foot are called Palanquin Way, the way the king obtains sport and roaming; Han’s palanquin way linked south and north palaces—this is its image.
translations.idiomatic: Five western stars are the Palanquin Way—the emperor’s pleasure road, like the Han gallery that joined the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 左右角間二星曰平道之官。

translations.literal: Two stars between left and right horns are the officials of the Level Road.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars between the horns are the Level Road judges.

sentences.zh: 平道西一星曰進賢，主卿相舉逸-{才}-。

translations.literal: One star west of Level Road is called Advancing Worthies, governing ministers and chancellors raising reclusive talent.
translations.idiomatic: West of them Advancing Worthies marks recommendations of hidden talent.

sentences.zh: 亢、東-{咸}-、西-{咸}-各四星，在房心北，日月五星之道也。

translations.literal: Kang, East Barrier, and West Barrier, four stars each, are north of Room and Heart, the road of sun, moon, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and the east and west barriers—four stars each north of Room and Heart—are the ecliptic gateway.

sentences.zh: 房之戸，所以防淫佚也。

translations.literal: They are the doors of Room, thereby guarding against dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: They are the bolt on Room’s door against excess.

sentences.zh: 星明則吉；

translations.literal: When the stars are bright, auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Bright barrier stars are good;

sentences.zh: 月、五星犯守之，有陰謀。

translations.literal: when moon and five planets invade and guard them, there is secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: moon or planets lingering there hint at conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 鍵閉一星，在房東北，近鉤鈐，主關籥。

translations.literal: One star Key and Lock is northeast of Room, near Hook and Hasp, governing bolts and keys.
translations.idiomatic: Key-and-Lock northeast of Room, by Hook-Hasp, rules bolts and keys.

sentences.zh: 天市垣二十二星，在房心東北，主權衡，主聚衆。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Market wall twenty-two stars are northeast of Room and Heart, governing beam-scale and gathering multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two stars of the Celestial Market northeast of Room and Heart mean trade and crowds.

sentences.zh: 一曰天旗庭，主斬戮之事也。

translations.literal: One name is Celestial Banner Court, governing beheading and slaughter affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the banner court of executions.

sentences.zh: 市中星衆潤澤，則歳實。

translations.literal: When stars in the market are many and lustrous, the harvest is solid.
translations.idiomatic: A thick bright throng in the market means a full harvest.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守之，戮不忠之臣。

translations.literal: When Mars guards it, disloyal ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Mars stationed there beheads faithless ministers.

sentences.zh: 彗星除之，爲徙市易都。

translations.literal: When a broom star sweeps it, there is moving the market and changing the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A comet sweeping it means markets move and capitals shift.

sentences.zh: 客星入之，兵大起；

translations.literal: When a guest star enters, great armies rise;
translations.idiomatic: A guest star entering sparks great war;

sentences.zh: 出之，有貴喪。

translations.literal: when it exits, there is noble mourning.
translations.idiomatic: its exit, mourning among the great.

sentences.zh: 帝坐一星，在天市中候星西，天庭也。

translations.literal: One star Imperial Seat is west of the Guard Star in the celestial market, the celestial court.
translations.idiomatic: The lone Imperial Seat west of the market’s guard star is heaven’s market throne.

sentences.zh: 光而潤則天子吉，威令行。

translations.literal: When lustrous and moist then the Son of Heaven is auspicious and awesome orders proceed.
translations.idiomatic: A soft bright glow means the sovereign thrives and commands bite.

sentences.zh: 候一星，在帝坐東北，主伺陰陽也。

translations.literal: One star Guard is northeast of Imperial Seat, governing watching yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Guard northeast of the throne watches yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 明大，輔臣強，四夷開；

translations.literal: When bright and large, supporting ministers are strong and the four Yi open;
translations.idiomatic: Large brightness means strong aides and open frontiers;

sentences.zh: 候細微，則國安；

translations.literal: when Guard is fine and subtle, then the state is secure;
translations.idiomatic: a faint steady Guard means peace;

sentences.zh: 亡則主失位；

translations.literal: when gone, the ruler loses position;
translations.idiomatic: if it vanishes, the ruler loses his seat;

sentences.zh: 移則不安。

translations.literal: when shifted, there is insecurity.
translations.idiomatic: if it drifts, the throne is uneasy.

sentences.zh: 宦者四星，在帝坐西南，侍主刑-{餘}-之人也。

translations.literal: Four stars of the palace attendant are southwest of Imperial Seat, attending the ruler, the class of those mutilated in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Four eunuch stars southwest serve the mutilated attendants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 星微，吉；

translations.literal: When stars are subtle, auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Faint eunuch stars are good;

sentences.zh: 非其常，宦者有憂。

translations.literal: when not according to their constant, palace attendants have worry.
translations.idiomatic: unusual brilliance alarms the inner servants.

sentences.zh: 宗正二星，在帝坐東南，宗大夫也。

translations.literal: Two stars of Director of the Imperial Clan are southeast of Imperial Seat, the clan grandees.
translations.idiomatic: Two Director of Clan stars southeast manage the royal house.

sentences.zh: 彗星守之，若失色，宗正有事；

translations.literal: When a comet guards them, or if they lose color, the director of the clan has affairs;
translations.idiomatic: A comet or dimming means trouble for the clan director;

sentences.zh: 客星守之，更號令也。

translations.literal: when a guest star guards them, edicts change.
translations.idiomatic: a guest star there changes the court’s edicts.

sentences.zh: 宗人四星，在宗正東，主録親疎享祀。

translations.literal: Four stars of Clan Men are east of Director of the Imperial Clan, governing recording kin near and far and enjoying sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Four Clan Men east of him record kin and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 族人有序，則如綺文而明正。

translations.literal: When the clan people are ordered, then they are like patterned brocade, bright and correct.
translations.idiomatic: When kin ranks are orderly, the stars read like clear brocade.

sentences.zh: 動則天子親屬有變；

translations.literal: When they move, then the Son of Heaven’s kin have change;
translations.idiomatic: Motion means shock among the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 客星守之，貴人死。

translations.literal: when a guest star guards them, a noble dies.
translations.idiomatic: a guest star there kills a noble.

sentences.zh: 宗星二，在候星東，宗室之象，帝輔血脈之臣也。

translations.literal: Two Clan Stars are east of the Guard Star, image of the imperial house, ministers who are the emperor’s bloodline aides.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clan Stars east of Guard image kinsmen ministers.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，宗支不和。

translations.literal: When a guest star guards them, branches of the clan are not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star parked there splits the royal kindred.

sentences.zh: 天江四星，在尾北，主太陰。

translations.literal: Four stars of Celestial River are north of Tail, governing Grand Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Four Celestial River stars north of Tail govern the great yin of floods.

sentences.zh: 江星不具，天下津河關道不通。

translations.literal: When River stars are not complete, under Heaven ferries, rivers, and passes are not open.
translations.idiomatic: Broken river stars block roads and fords.

sentences.zh: 明若動搖，大水出，大兵起；

translations.literal: When bright as if shaking, great water comes forth and great armies rise;
translations.idiomatic: Bright trembling means deluge and mobilization;

sentences.zh: 參差則馬貴。

translations.literal: when uneven, horses are dear.
translations.idiomatic: uneven ranks make horses dear.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守之，有立主。

translations.literal: When Mars guards it, there is setting up a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Mars guarding it can mean a rival sovereign.

sentences.zh: 客星入之，河津絶。

translations.literal: When a guest star enters, river fords are cut.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star entering snaps river crossings.

sentences.zh: 天籥八星在南-{斗}-柄西，主關閉。

translations.literal: Eight stars of Heaven’s Key are west of the Southern Dipper’s handle, governing shutting and opening.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Heaven’s Key stars west of the handle bolt the passes.

sentences.zh: 建星六星在南-{斗}-北，亦曰天旗，天之都關也。

translations.literal: Six stars of Establishment are north of the Southern Dipper, also called Heaven’s Banner, Heaven’s capital barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Six Establishment stars north of the Dipper are the celestial banner and capital gate.

sentences.zh: 爲謀事，爲天鼓，爲天馬。

translations.literal: They are for plotting affairs, for Heaven’s drum, for Heaven’s horse.
translations.idiomatic: They mean counsel, the sky-drum, and the sky-horse.

sentences.zh: 南二星，天庫也。

translations.literal: The southern two stars are Heaven’s storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The southern pair is the celestial granary.

sentences.zh: 中央二星，市也，鈇鑕也。

translations.literal: The central two stars are the market, axe and chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: The middle pair is the market and headsman’s block.

sentences.zh: 上二星，旗跗也。

translations.literal: The upper two stars are the flag’s heel.
translations.idiomatic: The northern pair is the flag’s heel.

sentences.zh: -{斗}-建之間，三光道也。

translations.literal: Between Dipper and Establishment is the road of the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Between Dipper and Establishment runs the ecliptic road.

sentences.zh: 星動則衆勞。

translations.literal: When stars move, the multitude labors.
translations.idiomatic: Their motion burdens the people.

sentences.zh: 月暈之，蛟龍見，牛馬疫。

translations.literal: When the moon haloes them, dragons appear, oxen and horses have pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: A lunar halo there brings dragons in portent and plague among beasts.

sentences.zh: 月、五星犯之，大臣相譖有謀，亦爲關梁不通，有大水。

translations.literal: When moon and five planets invade them, great ministers slander one another and plot, also meaning passes and bridges are not open and there is great water.
translations.idiomatic: Moon or five planets trespassing mean ministerial intrigue, blocked roads, and great floods.

sentences.zh: 東南四星曰狗國，主鮮卑、鳥丸、沃且。

translations.literal: Four southeastern stars are called Dog Country, governing Xianbei, Wuhuan, and Woju.
translations.idiomatic: Four southeast stars are Dog Country—Xianbei, Wuhuan, and Woju tribes.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守之，外夷爲變。

translations.literal: When Mars guards them, outer Yi change.
translations.idiomatic: Mars stationed there stirs the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 狗國北二星曰天鷄，主候時。

translations.literal: Two stars north of Dog Country are called Heaven’s Cock, governing watching the hours.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars north are the Sky Cock that crows the watches.

sentences.zh: 天弁九星，在建星北，市官之長也，以知市珍也。

translations.literal: Nine stars of Heaven’s Cap are north of Establishment Star, chief of market officers, thereby knowing market treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Sky Cap stars north of Establishment head the market inspectors.

sentences.zh: 星欲明，吉。

translations.literal: The stars desire to be bright, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They should burn bright—then trade thrives.

sentences.zh: 彗星犯守之，糴貴，囚徒起兵。

translations.literal: When a comet invades and guards them, grain is dear and convicts raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: A comet on them raises grain prices and jailbreak revolts.

sentences.zh: 河鼓三星，旗九星，在牽牛北，天鼓也，主軍鼓，主鈇鉞。

translations.literal: Three stars of River Drum, nine stars of Banner, are north of Herd-Boy, Heaven’s drum, governing army drums, governing axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Three River Drum stars and nine banner stars north of Altair are heaven’s war drum and regalia.

sentences.zh: 一曰三武，主天子三將軍；

translations.literal: One name is Three Martial, governing the Son of Heaven’s three generals;
translations.idiomatic: Called the Three Martial stars—the three field marshals;

sentences.zh: 中央大星爲大將軍，左星爲左將軍，右星爲右將軍。

translations.literal: the central great star is great general, left star is left general, right star is right general.
translations.idiomatic: the bright center is the commander-in-chief, flanked by left and right generals.

sentences.zh: 左星，南星也，所以備關梁而距難也，設守陰險，知謀徽也。

translations.literal: The left star is the southern star, thereby preparing passes and bridges and warding off difficulty, setting guards at yin narrows, knowing stratagems and signals.
translations.idiomatic: The left star guards the southern passes, blocks defiles, and reads stratagem.

sentences.zh: 旗即天鼓之旗，所以爲旌表也。

translations.literal: The banner is Heaven Drum’s banner, thereby serving as signal standard.
translations.idiomatic: The banner is the drum corps’ standard.

sentences.zh: 左旗九星，在鼓左旁。

translations.literal: Left banner nine stars are beside the drum on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Nine left-banner stars flank the drum.

sentences.zh: 鼓欲正直而明，色黃光澤，將吉；

translations.literal: The drum desires to be straight, correct, and bright, color yellow and lustrous—then generals are auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: The drum should stand straight, yellow, and glossy—then generals prosper;

sentences.zh: 不正，爲兵憂也。

translations.literal: not correct means worry of arms.
translations.idiomatic: crooked, expect military trouble.

sentences.zh: 星怒，馬貴。

translations.literal: When stars are angry, horses are dear.
translations.idiomatic: Angry stars make horses costly.

sentences.zh: 動則兵起，-{曲}-則將失計奪勢。

translations.literal: When they move then troops rise; when bent then generals lose plan and wrest power.
translations.idiomatic: Motion means war; a bent drum means generals lose their grip.

sentences.zh: 旗星差戾，亂相陵。

translations.literal: When banner stars are awry and harsh, chaos mutually encroaches.
translations.idiomatic: A skewed banner means factions claw one another.

sentences.zh: 旗端四星南北列，曰天桴，鼓桴也。

translations.literal: Four stars at the banner tip, arrayed north-south, are called Heaven’s Beater, the drumstick.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars at the banner tip are the drumsticks.

sentences.zh: 星不明，漏刻失時。

translations.literal: When stars are not bright, clepsydra loses the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Dim beaters throw the water-clock off.

sentences.zh: 前近河鼓，若桴鼓相直，皆爲桴鼓用。

translations.literal: Those near River Drum ahead, if beater and drum are mutually straight, all are for beater and drum use.
translations.idiomatic: Stars aligned with drum and stick mean the signal corps is active.

sentences.zh: 離珠五星，在須女北，須女之藏府，女子之星也。

translations.literal: Five stars of Pearls Apart are north of Maid, Maid’s treasury, stars of women.
translations.idiomatic: Five Pearls Apart north of Maid are the woman’s treasury stars.

sentences.zh: 天津九星，橫河中，一曰天漢，一曰天江，主四瀆津梁，所以度神通四方也。

translations.literal: Nine stars of Celestial Ford lie athwart the river; one name is Celestial River, one name Celestial Ford, governing the four channels’ fords and bridges, thereby ferrying spirits and penetrating the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Celestial Ford stars span the Milky Way—the great crossing of spirits and trade.

sentences.zh: 一星不備，津關道不通。

translations.literal: When one star is not prepared, fords and passes are not open.
translations.idiomatic: A missing star blocks the fords.

sentences.zh: 騰蛇二十二星，在營室北，天蛇也，主水-{蟲}-。

translations.literal: Twenty-two stars of Soaring Serpent are north of Encampment, Heaven’s serpent, governing water creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two Soaring Serpent stars north of House are the celestial snake of water beasts.

sentences.zh: 王良五星，在奎北，居河中，天子奉車-{御}-官也。

translations.literal: Five stars of Wang Liang are north of Legs, dwelling in the river, the Son of Heaven’s chariot officer.
translations.idiomatic: Five Wang Liang stars north of Legs in the stream are the royal charioteer.

sentences.zh: 其四星曰天駟，旁一星曰王良，亦曰天馬。

translations.literal: Its four stars are called Heaven’s Team; one star at the side is called Wang Liang, also called Heaven’s Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Four are the heavenly team; the side star is Wang Liang, also the sky-horse.

sentences.zh: 其星動，爲策馬，車騎滿野。

translations.literal: When its stars move, it is for whipping horses; chariots and riders fill the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: When they twitch, chariots stampede across the fields.

sentences.zh: 亦曰梁，爲天橋，主-{禦}-風雨水道，故或占車騎，或占津梁。

translations.literal: Again it is called Bridge, Heaven’s bridge, governing guarding against wind and rain on water roads; therefore sometimes divined for chariots and riders, sometimes for bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the sky bridge—wind and rain on waterways—read for cavalry or crossings alike.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，橋不通道。

translations.literal: When a guest star guards it, bridges do not open passage.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star there snaps the bridge.

sentences.zh: 前一星曰策星，王良之-{御}-策也，主天子之-{僕}-，在王良旁。

translations.literal: The forward one star is called Whip Star, Wang Liang’s chariot whip, governing the Son of Heaven’s runners, beside Wang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The lead star is the whip beside Wang Liang—the sovereign’s outriders.

sentences.zh: 若移在馬-{後}-，是謂策馬，則車騎滿野。

translations.literal: If it shifts behind the horse, that is called whipping horses, then chariots and riders fill the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: If it slips behind the team, the whip is raised and hosts ride.

sentences.zh: 閣道六星，在王良前，飛道也。

translations.literal: Six stars of Gallery Road are before Wang Liang, flying road.
translations.idiomatic: Six Gallery Road stars before Wang Liang are the flying causeway.

sentences.zh: 從紫宮至河，神所乘也，一曰，閣道星，天子-{遊}-別宮之道也。

translations.literal: From Purple Palace to River, what spirits ride; one name is Gallery Road stars, the Son of Heaven’s road for roaming separate palaces.
translations.idiomatic: They run from purple court to river—the spirit road, or the emperor’s gallery to detached palaces.

sentences.zh: 傅路一星，在閣道南，旁別道也。

translations.literal: One star Relay Road is south of Gallery Road, a side bypass road.
translations.idiomatic: One Relay Road star south is a bypass lane.

sentences.zh: 東壁北十星曰天廄，主馬之官，若今驛亭也，主傳令置驛，逐漏馳騖，謂其行急疾，興晷漏競馳也。

translations.literal: Ten stars north of eastern Wall are called Heaven’s Stable, office of horses, like today’s post stations, governing transmitting orders, setting relays, chasing clepsydra and galloping—called their movement swift and urgent, rising to race the sundial and clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Ten north of eastern Wall are Heaven’s Stables—relay posts that race the clock.

sentences.zh: 天將軍十二星，在婁北，主武兵。

translations.literal: Twelve stars of Heaven’s General are north of Bond, governing martial troops.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Heaven’s General stars north of Bond command armies.

sentences.zh: 中央大星，天之大將也。

translations.literal: The central great star is Heaven’s great general.
translations.idiomatic: The bright center is the supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 南一星曰軍南門，主誰何出入。

translations.literal: One southern star is called Army South Gate, governing challenging and inspecting exit and entry.
translations.idiomatic: The south star is the army gate sergeant who challenges all comers.

sentences.zh: 太陵八星在胃北，亦曰積京，主大喪也。

translations.literal: Eight stars of Great Tomb are north of Stomach, also called Stacked Capital, governing great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Great Tomb stars north of Stomach are stacked capital—great funerals.

sentences.zh: 積京中星衆，則諸侯有喪，民多疾，兵起。

translations.literal: When stars within Stacked Capital are many, the feudal lords have mourning, the people many sickness, troops rise.
translations.idiomatic: A crowded tomb means lords die, plagues spread, and armies stir.

sentences.zh: 太陵中一星曰積尸，明則死人如山。

translations.literal: One star within Great Tomb is called Stacked Corpses; when bright, dead men are like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Stacked Corpses star blazing means corpses pile like hills.

sentences.zh: 北九星曰天船，一曰舟星，所以濟不通也。

translations.literal: Nine northern stars are called Heaven’s Boat, one name Boat Stars, thereby ferrying what does not connect.
translations.idiomatic: Nine northern Boat stars ferry blocked roads.

sentences.zh: 中一星曰積水，候水災。

translations.literal: One central star is called Stacked Water, watching water disasters.
translations.idiomatic: The central Stacked Water star forecasts floods.

sentences.zh: 昴西二星曰天街，三光之道，主伺候關梁中外之境。

translations.literal: Two stars west of Hairy Head are called Celestial Street, road of the three luminaries, governing waiting on passes and bridges at inner and outer borders.
translations.idiomatic: Two Celestial Street stars west of Hairy Head mark the ecliptic frontier patrol.

sentences.zh: -{卷}-舌六星，在昴北，主口語，以知侫讒也。

translations.literal: Six stars of Rolled Tongue are north of Hairy Head, governing speech, thereby knowing flattery and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Six Rolled Tongue stars north of Hairy Head govern rumor and slander.

translations.literal: Curved, auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: A curled tongue is safe;

sentences.zh: 直而動，天下有口舌之害。

translations.literal: straight and moving, under Heaven there is harm of mouth and tongue.
translations.idiomatic: straight and twitching, slander poisons the realm.

sentences.zh: 中一星曰天讒，主巫醫。

translations.literal: One central star is called Heaven’s Slander, governing shamans and physicians.
translations.idiomatic: The center is Heaven’s Slander over witch doctors.

sentences.zh: 五車五星，三柱九星，在畢北。

translations.literal: Five Chariots five stars, three Pillars nine stars, are north of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Five chariot stars and nine pillar stars sit north of Net.

sentences.zh: 五車者，五帝車-{舍}-也，五帝坐也，主天子五兵，一曰主五-{穀}--{豐}-耗。

translations.literal: Five Chariots are the five thearchs’ chariot lodges, the five thearchs’ seats, governing the Son of Heaven’s five weapons; one name is governing the five grains’ abundance or waste.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Chariots are the five emperors’ garages—arms and grain in one emblem.

sentences.zh: 西北大星曰天庫，主太白，主秦。

translations.literal: The great northwest star is called Heaven’s Storehouse, governing Grand White, governing Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest bright star is the vault of Venus and Qin.

sentences.zh: 次東北星曰獄，主辰星，主燕趙。

translations.literal: The next northeast star is called Prison, governing Chronograph Star, governing Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast next is Prison of Mercury over Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 次東星曰天倉，主歳星，主魯衞。

translations.literal: The next eastern star is called Heaven’s Granary, governing Year Star, governing Lu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern granary holds Jupiter over Lu and Wei.

sentences.zh: 次東南星曰司空，主塡星，主楚。

translations.literal: The next southeast star is called Minister of Works, governing Saturn, governing Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast is Minister of Works and Saturn over Chu.

sentences.zh: 次西南星曰卿星，主熒惑，主魏。

translations.literal: The next southwest star is called Minister Star, governing Mars, governing Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest is Minister Star and Mars over Wei.

sentences.zh: 五星有變，皆以其所主占之。

translations.literal: When the five stars have change, all are divined according to what they govern.
translations.idiomatic: Each chariot star is read for its planet and region.

sentences.zh: 三柱一曰三泉。

translations.literal: The three Pillars, one name is Three Springs.
translations.idiomatic: The three pillars are also called Three Springs.

sentences.zh: 天子得靈-{臺}-之禮，則五車、三柱均明有常。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven obtains the rites of Spirit Terrace, then Five Chariots and Three Pillars are evenly bright with constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Proper Spirit Terrace rites keep chariots and pillars steadily bright.

sentences.zh: 其中五星曰天潢。

translations.literal: Within them five stars are called Celestial Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Five inner stars form the Celestial Ford cluster.

sentences.zh: 天潢南三星曰-{咸}-池，魚囿也。

translations.literal: Three stars south of Celestial Ford are called Xian Pool, fish preserve.
translations.idiomatic: Three south of the ford are Xian Pool—the royal fishpond.

sentences.zh: 月、五星入天潢，兵起，道不通，天下亂。

translations.literal: When moon and five planets enter Celestial Ford, troops rise, roads are not open, under Heaven is chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Moon or planets in the ford mean war, blocked roads, and chaos.

sentences.zh: 五車南六星曰諸王，察諸侯存亡。

translations.literal: Six stars south of Five Chariots are called Many Princes, inspecting the feudal lords’ survival or perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Six Many Princes stars south watch the fiefs live or die.

sentences.zh: 其西八星曰八-{穀}-，主候歳。

translations.literal: Its western eight stars are called Eight Grains, governing watching the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Eight western Eight Grains stars forecast the crop.

sentences.zh: 八-{穀}-一星亡，一-{穀}-不登。

translations.literal: When one star of Eight Grains perishes, one grain does not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Each lost star is a failed crop.

sentences.zh: 天關一星，在五車南，亦曰天門，日月之所行也，主邊事，主關閉。

translations.literal: One star Celestial Pass is south of Five Chariots, also called Heaven’s Gate, where sun and moon travel, governing border affairs, governing shutting and opening.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Pass south of the chariots is the sun-moon gate of frontier open-shut.

sentences.zh: 芒角，有兵。

translations.literal: Awn and horns—there are troops.
translations.idiomatic: Comet hair on it means arms.

sentences.zh: 五星守之，貴人多死。

translations.literal: When the five planets guard it, many nobles die.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets lingering slay many grandees.

sentences.zh: 東井鉞前四星曰司怪，主候天地日月星辰變異及鳥獸草木之妖，明主聞災，修德保福也。

translations.literal: Four stars east of Well’s axe-head are called Director of Prodigies, governing watching heaven, earth, sun, moon, stars, and constellations’ anomalies and birds, beasts, and plants’ prodigies; when bright the ruler hears disaster and cultivates virtue to preserve blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Four Director of Prodigies east of the well-axe watch omens so the king may mend his virtue.

sentences.zh: 司怪西北九星曰坐旗，君臣設位之表也。

translations.literal: Nine stars northwest of Director of Prodigies are called Seated Banner, the surface where lord and ministers set ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Seated Banner stars northwest mark the court lineup.

sentences.zh: 坐旗西四星曰天髙，-{臺}-謝之髙，主遠望氣象。

translations.literal: Four stars west of Seated Banner are called Celestial Height, height of terrace ascension, governing watching far and inspecting vapors and images.
translations.idiomatic: Four Celestial Height stars west are the high watchtower for vapors.

sentences.zh: 天髙西一星曰天河，主察山林妖變。

translations.literal: One star west of Celestial Height is called Celestial River, governing inspecting mountain forests’ prodigious changes.
translations.idiomatic: One Celestial River west scans woodland portents.

sentences.zh: 南河、北河各三星，夾東井。

translations.literal: South River and North River, three stars each, flank Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: South and North Rivers—three stars each—bracket the Well.

sentences.zh: 一曰天髙，天之關門也，主關梁。

translations.literal: One name is Celestial Height, Heaven’s barrier gate, governing passes and bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Also called heaven’s barrier of fords.

sentences.zh: 南河曰南戍，一曰南宮，一曰陽門，一曰越門，一曰權星，主火。

translations.literal: South River is called South Guard, one name South Palace, one name Yang Gate, one name Yue Gate, one name Power Star, governing fire.
translations.idiomatic: South River is the south guard, south palace, yang gate, Yue gate, power star—fire.

sentences.zh: 北河曰北戍，一曰北宮，一曰陰門，一曰胡門，一曰衡星，主水。

translations.literal: North River is called North Guard, one name North Palace, one name Yin Gate, one name Hu Gate, one name Balance Star, governing water.
translations.idiomatic: North River is the north guard, north palace, yin gate, Hu gate, balance star—water.

sentences.zh: 兩河戍間，日月五星之常道也。

translations.literal: Between the two river guards is the constant road of sun, moon, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Between them runs the planets’ highway.

sentences.zh: 河戍動搖，中國兵起。

translations.literal: When river guards shake, central states’ troops rise.
translations.idiomatic: Shaking river guards mobilize China.

sentences.zh: 南河南三星曰闕丘，主宮門外象魏也。

translations.literal: Three stars south of South River are called Gate Tower Mound, image of the palace gate’s outer drum tower.
translations.idiomatic: Three south of South River are Gate Tower Mound—the gate drum platform.

sentences.zh: 五諸侯五星，在東井北，主刺舉，戒不虞。

translations.literal: Five stars of Five Feudatories are north of Eastern Well, governing impeachment, guarding against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Five Feudatories north of the Well impeach treason and watch surprise.

sentences.zh: 又曰理陰陽，察得失。

translations.literal: Again called ordering yin and yang, inspecting gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: They also balance yin-yang and weigh fault.

sentences.zh: 亦曰主帝心。

translations.literal: Again called governing the emperor’s mind.
translations.idiomatic: They image the emperor’s inner council.

sentences.zh: 一曰帝師，二曰帝友，三曰三公，四曰博士，五曰太史，此五者常爲帝定疑議。

translations.literal: One is imperial teacher, two imperial friend, three three dukes, four erudite, five grand scribe—these five constantly settle the emperor’s doubts and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Five roles—teacher, friend, three dukes, erudite, scribe—settle the ruler’s doubts.

sentences.zh: 星明大潤澤，則天下大治；

translations.literal: When stars are bright, large, and lustrous, then under Heaven is greatly ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Bright moist stars mean great order;

sentences.zh: 芒角，則禍在中。

translations.literal: awn and horns, then calamity is in the center.
translations.idiomatic: comet hair means disaster at court.

sentences.zh: 五諸侯南三星曰天樽，主盛饘粥以給貧餒。

translations.literal: Three stars south of Five Feudatories are called Celestial Goblet, governing filling gruel to give the starving.
translations.idiomatic: Three Celestial Goblet stars south ladle gruel for the hungry.

sentences.zh: 積水一星，在北河西北，水河也，所以供酒食之正也。

translations.literal: One star Stacked Water is northwest of North River, water river, thereby supplying correctness of drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: Stacked Water northwest of North River is the wine stream of banquets.

sentences.zh: 積薪一星在積水東北，供庖廚之正也。
